User.title: User

name.description: The full name of the user.

dateJoined.description: The date and time the user joined the application.

LearningPath.title: LearningPath
LearningPath.description: Represents a personalized learning path for a user.

id.description: Unique identifier for the learning path.

userId.description: Reference to the User. (Relationship: User 1:N LearningPath)

name.description: The name of the learning path.

description.description: A description of the learning path.

createdAt.description: The date and time the learning path was created.

Progress.title: Progress
Progress.description: Represents the progress of a user on a learning path.

id.description: Unique identifier for the progress entry.

userId.description: Reference to the User. (Relationship: User 1:N Progress)

learningPathId.description: Reference to the LearningPath. (Relationship: LearningPath 1:N Progress)

date.description: The date of the progress entry.

percentageComplete.description: The percentage of the learning path that is complete.

type.description: The type of resource (e.g., video, article, book).

Recommendation.title: Recommendation
Recommendation.description: Represents a learning resource recommendation for a user.

userId.description: Reference to the User. (Relationship: User 1:N Recommendation)

resourceId.description: Reference to the Resource. (Relationship: Resource 1:N Recommendation)

firestore.reasoning:
This Firestore structure is designed to support the StudyAI application, focusing on storing user data, learning paths, progress, resources, and recommendations. The structure is optimized for security, scalability, and debuggability by adhering to the principles of Authorization Independence, Structural Segregation, and Access Modeling.

*   **Authorization Independence:** The structure leverages path-based ownership for user-specific data (learning paths, progress, recommendations).  No `get()` calls are needed in security rules to validate ownership.
*   **Structural Segregation:**  Each collection contains data with a homogenous security posture. User-specific data is kept separate from global data (resources).
*   **Access Modeling:** The structure uses path-based ownership for user-owned data, ensuring that only the user has access to their learning paths, progress, and recommendations. Resources are global.
*   **QAPs (Query Authorization Predictability):** Secure `list` operations are enabled by segregating data based on ownership. Listing learning paths, progress entries, or recommendations is always scoped to a specific user ID in the path.

The weekly progress graph requirement is addressed by the `/users/{userId}/progress/{progressId}` structure. Each progress document is a snapshot of a user's learning path progress at a specific date. This detailed structure makes it easy to query and aggregate data for weekly progress visualization.

The suggested resources feature is facilitated by the `/recommendations/{recommendationId}` collection. The structure includes a `userId` and `resourceId` for easy querying and filtering, adhering to QAPs.
